tier_reason: Peer-reviewed SC19 paper (ACM DOI 10.1145/3295500.3356181, Best Student Paper, linked from the README) plus README result tables naming CPU/GPU models (Xeon E5-2690 v3, Tesla P100) and baseline versions (MKL 19.0.1.144, LibSci 19.06.1, LibSci_acc 19.10.1); miniapps (miniapp/cosma_miniapp, pxgemm_miniapp) are public but compiler and flags are not stated, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README text: 'speedups by factor of up to 8.3x over the second-fastest algorithm' (no supporting table on the README). CP2K RPA 128-H2O on 1024 Piz Daint GPU nodes: the 46 pdgemm calls took 75.26 s with COSMA-GPU vs 139.82 s with Cray LibSci_acc 19.10.1 (README 'approximately 2x faster'; 1.86x derived from page data). On 128 nodes: CPU-only COSMA 1723.62 s vs Intel MKL 19.0.1.144 ScaLAPACK 1836.85 s vs Cray LibSci 5896.45 s for the pdgemm calls (1.07x over MKL derived from page data; table annotation '~10% faster'; whole CP2K run 2238.94 s vs 2305.41 s), COSMA-GPU 257.99 s vs LibSci_acc 338.47 s (1.31x derived from page data; README '25-27% faster than the second best'). Square matrices on 128 nodes vs MKL ScaLAPACK: plot annotated '~2x faster on CPU' (about 300 vs 150 GFlop/s at n=20000, narrowing to about 740 vs 565 at n=120000, read from plot) and '~3x faster on GPU' (GPU COSMA vs CPU-only MKL).
corrections.hardware: Piz Daint: CP2K runs on Cray XC50 GPU-partition nodes (Intel Xeon E5-2690 v3 @ 2.60GHz 12 cores, NVIDIA Tesla P100 16GB), 128 and 1024 nodes; square-matrix runs on 128 XC50 (GPU) and XC40 (CPU-only) nodes
corrections.caveats: Peer-reviewed (SC19 Best Student Paper; ACM DL and arXiv:1908.09606 linked from README) but the paper could not be opened in this run (arxiv.org and mirrors blocked); its abstract, seen only as a web-search snippet, reports up to 12.8x (2.2x on average) over ScaLAPACK, CARMA and CTF, while the README says up to 8.3x over the second-fastest algorithm. Against MKL ScaLAPACK in the CP2K workload the CPU win is small (about 7% on pdgemm time, 3% on total run time); the 2x and 3x figures are against Cray LibSci_acc or compare GPU COSMA with CPU-only MKL. README result tables are SVG/plot images. Compiler and flags not stated; results are from 2019 with MKL 19.0.1.144, Cray LibSci 19.06.1 and LibSci_acc 19.10.1.

notes: README tables (rendered from docs/*.svg) confirm the 2x and 25-27% claims; the record's numbers were correct but the MKL margin in the production workload is only about 7%. Metadata verified: BSD-3-Clause, 219 stars, not archived, last commit 2026-07-29.

tier_reason: First-party BENCHMARKS.md with public benchmark programs (bench_qr_compact, bench_posv_compact) and gcc -O3 -march=native, but the hardware is only a '4-core AVX-512 container' with no CPU model, so not A.

corrections.caveats: Hardware is not identified beyond '4-core AVX-512 container', so tier C; the benchmark page labels the runs 'indicative'; pack/unpack time is excluded from the timed region; per-matrix LAPACK wins from about n=128-168 (0.25x at n=256) and at nrhs=64 is level or ahead at several sizes (0.85-0.95x at n=80 and 120); SPD solve only matches MKL compact. The benchmarks build only with -DCBK_WITH_MKL=ON, under which the per-matrix LAPACKE baseline is MKL's own LAPACKE (sequential MKL) per docs/building.md. Compact routines do not check lwork, so an undersized workspace is an out-of-bounds write (documented). The README states most of the library, tests and benchmarks were written by Claude models with human review.

notes: All numbers in claimed_speedup match examples/BENCHMARKS.md; the Notes section also gives 2.8x geomean for gels vs LAPACKE_dgels at 4 threads (7.7x at n=10, 1.4x at n=120). Metadata verified: Apache-2.0, 1 star, last commit 2026-09-15.

tier_reason: Upgraded: benchmark source is public (bench/dgemmtest.c and bench/sgemmtest.c, which dlopen the user library and time it against statically linked MKL 2019u4, with an example gcc compile command), the library Makefile states gcc -fopenmp -march=haswell -O2, and the CPU is named (i9-9900K, AVX offset 6, 8 threads).

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: SGEMM 963-976 GFLOPS (MKL2019: 944-951), DGEMM 477-481 GFLOPS (MKL2019: 466-469) at M=N=K=20000, 8 threads, i.e. about 2-3% faster (derived from page data). Bench screenshots: DGEMM 20000 NN MKL 467.1-468.0 vs library 478.9-480.5 GFLOPS; SGEMM 45000 NN MKL 942.5-942.7 vs library 996.0-997.5 GFLOPS (about 5.8% faster, derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Library: gcc -fopenmp --shared -fPIC -march=haswell -O2 (Makefile); bench harness: gcc -fopenmp with static MKL (mkl_intel_lp64, mkl_gnu_thread, mkl_core) per the comment in bench/dgemmtest.c; compiler version not stated
corrections.caveats: Margin is small (2-3% at n=20000, about 6% for SGEMM at n=45000 in a screenshot) and measured on one overclocked desktop CPU (i9-9900K, AVX offset 6); MKL is the GNU-threaded build (libgomp), not Intel OpenMP; compiler version not stated; prebuilt test binaries are shipped beside the sources. The bench program checks the result against MKL (max abs difference about 1e-11 for DGEMM). Repo archived on 2019-08-27. Successor repo wjc404/GEMM_AVX2 says it can 'outperform Intel MKL (2019 update 4) after tuning', and wjc404/GEMM_AVX512F says '99% MKL 1-thread performance after tuning' (not faster).

notes: Tier raised C to A because bench source, Makefile flags and CPU model are all public; margin is only a few percent, so treat as parity-plus. Metadata verified: GPL-3.0, 1 star, archived 2019-08-27, last commit 2019-08-27; successor-repo statements in caveats were not re-checked.
